messages:
maria: Heads-up — the role-schema backfill ran at 03:12 UTC and I'm seeing an uptick in 403s for a subset of service accounts, specifically ones created before 2022.
raj: Which permission is missing? any pattern in affected resources?
dave: Looks like `project.read` is missing on billing projects. Repro locally by impersonating a service account: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=sa-old@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com)' https://api.redwood.ai/projects/123` returns 403.
leah: Confirmed. Audit logs show a backfill job writing `default_role_id = NULL` for rows where `role_assigned_at IS NULL`.
maria: Exactly — the backfill script attempted to set defaults but skipped rows with legacy role foreign-key values. Suspect FK constraint mismatch with new `roles_v2` ids.
raj: Can we get a quick query to list affected svc accounts? I can run a targeted fix.
dave: `SELECT sa.email FROM service_accounts sa JOIN membership m ON m.principal_id = sa.id WHERE m.role_id IS NULL AND sa.created_at < '2022-01-01';` — that's the set I'm seeing.
leah: Proposed mitigation: 1) pause any further backfills, 2) run a one-off fix to map legacy role names to new role ids for NULLs, 3) re-run backfill in canary mode.
maria: Agreed. Also want to check KMS: some customer-managed keys were referenced during the migration (we rotated cmk metadata). If any service account lost access to KMS keys it could surface as 403s too.
audit-bot: [ALERT] role-backfill-job-2026-03-20 created 128 role-null events. Correlation id: c8f7b2. More at https://console.redwood.ai/audit/c8f7b2
raj: @deploy-bot can you pause schedule for `role-backfill-job-2026-03-20`? We should avoid ripping more defaults.
deploy-bot: Pausing scheduled job `role-backfill-job-2026-03-20` — triggered by @raj. Job state: paused.
dave: Quick remediation SQL I'd run on a canary DB:

```
BEGIN;
UPDATE membership m
SET role_id = r.id
FROM roles r
WHERE m.role_id IS NULL AND r.name = 'project-reader'::text AND m.principal_type = 'service_account';
-- verify rowcount then COMMIT;
ROLLBACK;
```

Run with `RETURNING` on a staging copy first.
leah: We'll also need to regenerate role hashes used by the auth cache and flush cache on auth-gateway.
maria: After canary success, plan: 1) map legacy role names -> new ids for NULL rows, 2) run in waves by created_at, 3) monitor `auth.403.rate` + `audit:roles.null` metric, 4) postmortem.
raj: Assigning owners: db fix -> dave, auth cache flush -> leah, rollout coord -> maria. I'll take communications to CSMs for any customer-facing incidents.
dave: On it. I'll prepare a rollback patch if mapping reveals collisions. Expect a canary run in ~30m.
maria: Thanks. If anyone sees unexpected KMS permission errors include `kms_key_id` in the audit link. We'll triage separately.
leah: Adding runbook note: when `role_id IS NULL` after backfill, do NOT delete membership rows; prefer mapping -> role to avoid accidental privilege removal. :warning:
maria: Good call. Let's sync on voice if canary shows >5% error increase. Otherwise post results here and I'll open a short postmortem template.
